entitlements.notes: Quota verified: "Unlimited complimentary Domestic airport lounge access in India with your HDFC Bank Infinia Credit Card (Primary & Add-on)." The PROGRAMME is not named, and HDFC’s own linked eligible-lounge list (lms.hoi.in/lounge-list/hdfc-infinia, backed by loungepass.hoi.in) returns an empty result set. Hidden until a source names the programme.

HDFC: "Unlimited complimentary International airport lounge access outside India via Priority Pass for Primary and Add-on cardholders (1,000+ lounges worldwide)." Correctly opens nothing at an Indian airport — the geography is the issuer’s own word.

HDFC states unlimited lounge access "India and worldwide" — the one card whose own wording covers both zones and both geographies. No programme is named beyond the Diners Club travel tool app, and no lounge in this directory is yet shown to accept a Diners-branded programme, so the row is hidden rather than matched on a guess.

spendGate.summary: if you spent ₹60,000 in the previous quarter

entitlements.notes: One of only two places any issuer names DreamFolks in a sentence (the other is Axis Atlas). 3 domestic visits per calendar quarter, gated on ₹60,000 spend in the preceding quarter — the gate itself lives in the milestones dataset and is referenced, not copied. HDFC’s marketing tile separately says "6 Complimentary domestic lounge visits outside India", which is self-contradicting; the terms were taken over the tile.
6 international visits a calendar year, outside India, via Priority Pass. Opens nothing at an Indian terminal.
4 international visits a calendar year, at most 1 a quarter, outside India, on the Visa variant via Priority Pass. Opens nothing at an Indian terminal.

HDFC: "12 Complimentary access within India (both at domestic and international terminals)" — twelve visits total across both zones, not twelve of each, which is what `scope` being a list exists for. The programme is named only as the Diners Club travel tool app, and no lounge here is yet shown to accept it, so the row stays hidden. HDFC’s Marriott lounge FAQ PDF could not be read (Firecrawl failed on all engines, WebFetch timed out); nothing is cited from it. The international count is stated only as "Complimentary access outside India every year" with no number — a "12 international" figure circulates on blogs and was deliberately not recorded.

Axis: "Eligible airport lounges at Indian international terminals after immigration are considered international lounges and can be accessed using your Priority Pass." Unlike HDFC, whose Priority Pass is complimentary only outside India. Reserve: unlimited international visits plus 12 complimentary guest visits a year. Guests are recorded as not counting against the cardholder's own visits because the guest allowance is stated separately.

Axis: "Eligible airport lounges at Indian international terminals after immigration are considered international lounges and can be accessed using your Priority Pass." Unlike HDFC, whose Priority Pass is complimentary only outside India. Olympus: unlimited international visits plus 10 complimentary guest visits an anniversary year. Its terms exist only as a PDF — no live Axis product page for Olympus was found, and two plausible slugs 404.

Axis names DreamFolks for Atlas domestic access in its T&C — one of only two places any issuer names DreamFolks in a sentence. Tier quotas are 8 / 12 / 18 domestic visits at ₹3L / ₹7.5L / ₹15L annual spend.
entitlements.assumption: Axis states the tier quotas with NO period attached. The base tier of 8 is shown over a calendar year, which is the usual reading, but Axis does not say so. The higher tiers are not modelled at all, because doing so would need the spend tier tracked and the period guessed twice over.

entitlements.notes: Quota read from Axis (unlimited domestic, gated on ₹50,000 spend in the previous 3 months). The PROGRAMME is not named, so which desks honour it is unread and the row stays hidden. Note also that the Magnus page still advertises domestic Priority Pass use, which the 28-08-2026 change appears to have ended — a second reason not to ship this row yet. Beware axisbank.com/retail/cards/credit-card/magnus-credit-card: it does not 404, it silently serves the Axis sitemap page.
ICICI states unlimited international lounge access via Priority Pass for Emeralde Private Metal.
entitlements.assumption: ICICI does not say whether its Priority Pass works at Indian international terminals. Axis says its own does and HDFC says its own does not, so the question is genuinely open. Recorded as worldwide, which is the reading that matches Priority Pass’s own programme rules, and shown as assumed so the screen says so.

entitlements.notes: ICICI: 2 international visits a year via Priority Pass. Its domestic figure is stated inconsistently — 4 per calendar quarter in one place, "2 per quarter for each variant" in another — so no domestic row ships for this card. Beware the slug: /sapphiro-credit-card serves the card LISTING page rather than a 404.
entitlements.assumption: Whether the Priority Pass works at Indian international terminals is not stated; recorded as worldwide and shown as assumed, the same reading as Emeralde.

entitlements.notes: ICICI: 1 domestic visit a calendar quarter, gated on ₹75,000 spend in the preceding calendar quarter. No international access at all. The programme is NOT named in any sentence — the page carries a DreamFolks logo asset only, which is suggestive and not a source — so the row stays hidden. Coral also grants 4 railway lounge visits a year, which this dataset does not model.

SBI: 6 international visits a calendar year, at most 2 a quarter, via Priority Pass. SBI’s own charges table has three columns — domestic within India, international within India, international outside India — and only the last is complimentary, so this opens nothing at an Indian terminal.

SBI: 2 domestic visits a quarter, fulfilled through the card NETWORKS (Visa / Mastercard / RuPay / American Express) rather than an aggregator — so the programme depends on which network the holder’s card carries, which one row cannot express. Hidden until the dataset can key a row to the card’s own network. SBI’s published domestic lounge lists also contain International T2/T3 rows, so its "domestic" entitlement may reach international terminals; unresolved.
SBI: 4 international visits a calendar year, at most 2 a quarter, outside India, via Priority Pass. PRIME is filed under /rewards/, not /lifestyle/ — the latter 404s.

SBI: 8 domestic visits a year, at most 2 a quarter, through the card networks rather than an aggregator. Hidden for the same reason as ELITE’s domestic row — the programme depends on the holder’s network.

Unlimited Priority Pass access outside India; inside India the same pass is chargeable at US$35 a visit, which is not complimentary access and is therefore not modelled as opening anything. Amex also grants its own Centurion, Delta Sky Club, Plaza Premium and Lufthansa lounges — none of those programmes is yet provable against a lounge in this directory. The card is a CHARGE card on a different URL path; /in/credit-cards/platinum-card.html is an Amex error page.
